submission.justification: Sensor-T1 has the best resolution (~6.0 um at 150 um) but is ruled out: its hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2 is 82.0% (2026 test beam), below the hard 97% requirement. Of the two that pass, T2 (98.5%) resolves much better than T3 (99.2%): about 9 um versus 14.2-14.9 um. A thickness scan of T2 shows a flat best region from roughly 100 to 175 um. Single runs gave 8.6-9.4 um, and repeat runs at the same point differ by about 0.4-0.6 um, which is simulation noise. Resolution gets clearly worse at 50 um (10.5 um) and at 200-300 um (9.2-12.2 um). Within that flat region I picked 150 um. It is in the middle, matches the 2025 reference simulations, and gave 9.37 and 8.65 um in two runs. Caveats: the test-beam document does not state the thickness of the irradiated samples, and all resolution numbers are for unirradiated sensors. Efficiency and resolution at 150 um after irradiation should be confirmed in the next campaign.

requirements.evidence: Best among technologies passing the efficiency limit: T2 at 150 um is about 9.0 um (8.65 and 9.37 um in two runs), versus 14.2 um for T3. T1 (6.0 um) fails the efficiency requirement. Simulation is unirradiated only.
